result:
The current implementation queues and records a webhook delivery, but **does not actually call the customer’s endpoint**. The delivery job computes a signature and logs the attempt, then marks the row delivered. That limitation also means there is no implemented retry of a failed HTTP request.

The path starts in [the new issue page](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/9ace707c-131e-4459-9429-758088020c63/src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/projects/[projectSlug]/issues/new/page.tsx), which passes `createIssueAction` to `IssueForm`. In [issue-form.tsx](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/9ace707c-131e-4459-9429-758088020c63/src/components/domain/issue/issue-form.tsx), the form validates against `createIssueSchema` and submits through `useFormAction`. [create-issue.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/9ace707c-131e-4459-9429-758088020c63/src/actions/issues/create-issue.ts) runs the server action through `withAction`, which validates again and resolves the actor. The action checks permission and the project’s issue quota, then calls `createIssue`.

In [issue-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/9ace707c-131e-4459-9429-758088020c63/src/server/services/issue-service.ts), `createIssue` checks organization scope, the project, permission and quota; allocates a number; and inserts the issue. It then awaits `emit("issue.created", …)`, with the actor envelope, issue and project IDs, title, assignee and priority. The in-process `emit` in [event-bus.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/9ace707c-131e-4459-9429-758088020c63/src/lib/event-bus.ts) waits for subscribers to settle but isolates their errors, so a failing webhook listener does not make issue creation fail.

The webhook listener is installed at Node server startup: `register` in [instrumentation.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/9ace707c-131e-4459-9429-758088020c63/src/instrumentation.ts) calls `registerEventHandlers` in [event-registry.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/9ace707c-131e-4459-9429-758088020c63/src/server/services/event-registry.ts), which calls `registerWebhookListeners`. Its `issue.created` handler in [webhook-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/9ace707c-131e-4459-9429-758088020c63/src/server/services/webhook-service.ts) serializes the event payload and calls `enqueueForOrg`. That function uses `listEndpoints` in [webhook-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/9ace707c-131e-4459-9429-758088020c63/src/server/repositories/webhook-repository.ts) to retrieve only that organization’s endpoints. It skips disabled endpoints and those whose stored event-type list does not include `issue.created`, then calls `enqueueDelivery` for each match. Each resulting database row starts as `pending`, with zero attempts.

Startup also calls `startScheduler` in [scheduler.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/9ace707c-131e-4459-9429-758088020c63/src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts). Its minute tick queues a `webhook-delivery` job; `drain` and `runHandler` in [queue.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/9ace707c-131e-4459-9429-758088020c63/src/server/jobs/queue.ts) invoke `runWebhookDeliveryJob`. The authenticated `POST` in [the cron route](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/9ace707c-131e-4459-9429-758088020c63/src/app/api/cron/webhook-delivery/route.ts) can invoke the same job directly.

In [webhook-delivery-job.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/9ace707c-131e-4459-9429-758088020c63/src/server/jobs/webhook-delivery-job.ts), `runWebhookDeliveryJob` claims up to 25 pending rows; `claimPendingDeliveries` increments each attempt count. The job checks that the organization still permits webhooks, that the attempt count has not exceeded six, and that the endpoint still exists and is enabled. Those failed checks mark the row `failed`. Otherwise, it calls `signPayload`, logs the URL and part of the signature, and calls `markDelivered`—there is no outbound HTTP request.

There is retry-related bookkeeping, but it does not implement the promised HTTP retry. `backoffMs` calculates 1, 2, 4 seconds and so on, capped at five minutes, but the delivery job only logs that value; it does not schedule a delivery using it. A row left pending after an interrupted job can be claimed again on a later pass, and a claim beyond six attempts is marked failed. Separately, `queue.ts` retries a *job handler that throws*, with exponential delay and a five-attempt limit; that is not an HTTP response retry.

For authenticity, `signPayload` in `webhook-service.ts` computes a hex-encoded HMAC-SHA256 over the exact UTF-8 payload string using the endpoint’s secret, generated by `createWebhook`. A receiver would need the same secret and the exact raw body to recompute and compare the signature. The current delivery job does not send a body or signature header, so that verification cannot yet happen for a real delivery. The `POST` test route in [api/webhooks/[endpointId]/test/route.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/9ace707c-131e-4459-9429-758088020c63/src/app/api/webhooks/[endpointId]/test/route.ts) does return a sample payload and its signature for checking the calculation, but it also does not call the endpoint.
